title: United Airlines 624
summary: United Airlines Flight 624, a Douglas DC-6, experienced a fire warning that prompted the crew to deploy the fire extinguisher system. However, the crew neglected to manually activate required cabin pressure relief valves before deployment. The concentrated CO2 gas incapacitated the crew in the cockpit, causing them to lose situational awareness. The incapacitated crew descended below minimum safe altitude and crashed into terrain near Mount Carmel, Pennsylvania, killing all 43 aboard. Investigation found no evidence of an actual fire.
probable_cause: Incapacitation of the crew by concentrated CO2 gas in the cockpit following erroneous fire warning and improper deployment of fire extinguisher system without activation of required pressure relief valves, causing loss of control and terrain impact.

factors.evidence: High workload during emergency procedures led to procedural deviation
Crew failed to activate pressure relief valves before deploying CO2 system
Concentrated CO2 gas incapacitated crew in cockpit
Incapacitated crew flew toward elevated terrain instead of suitable landing sites
Aircraft descended uncontrollably and crashed into hillside
Fire extinguisher system design allowed crew to incapacitate themselves

Aircraft descended uncontrollably while crew was incapacitated
